name: Heresy
overview: The Scriptures reveal that heresy, characterized by false teachings such as imposing circumcision and law-keeping contrary to the gospel, was a serious threat to the early church, as noted in Acts 15:24 where certain individuals troubled believers with such demands. Paul and Silas faced severe opposition and punishment, including accusations of disturbing the city and teaching unlawful customs (Acts 16:20-23), while Paul himself was accused of persuading people to worship God contrary to the law (Acts 18:13) but firmly denied these charges (Acts 24:13). The propagation and promotion of heresy were forbidden and met with harsh penalties, underscoring the early church’s commitment to preserving the truth of the gospel against falsehood.
